name: Three-dimensional computational model of brain injury biomechanics
description: A high-fidelity three-dimensional computational model of brain injury biomechanics, used to map strain and strain rate at the grey matter-white matter boundary for three head impacts: a helmet-to-helmet impact in American football, an occipital impact from a fall, and a helmeted impact in a road traffic accident. It predicted that strain is largest at the depths of sulci, where chronic traumatic encephalopathy pathology is seen.
spatial_context: Three-dimensional anatomy of the human head and brain, including the grey matter-white matter boundary.

references.title: Computational modelling of traumatic brain injury predicts the location of chronic traumatic encephalopathy pathology.

computational_method: Three-dimensional computational modelling of head impact
prediction_scope: Brain tissue strain and strain rate under a given head impact, and the fraction of sulcal and gyral regions exceeding brain injury thresholds. It does not model cellular injury or neurodegeneration.
